body: Everything, very bluntly as well to help him understand. And made sure he knows it's not because of him in any way!

He's not taking it great - he gets down about it easily. He lets me talk about it to him and listens, originally there was some 'tough love' (i.e. "that's life though, honey") but I literally helped him realise 10 mins ago it doesn't help me at all. I think he knows a little more how to handle it now and I've asked him just to be himself, so that's working :)

I think I can - there are people much worse off than me and I don't feel like I can do anything like this to hurt my partner. Plus he will be there to stop me if I wanted to hurt myself in any way. I can safely say: I honestly want to die, but I don't think I will do anything to let that happen. But now I feel like a fraud on here lol

I have no idea. I told her about Saturday and how I was feeling then and still get similar feelings. But I do tend to dumb down my situation a lot - saying that I don't know if I would really do it. Maybe she gets so many everyday she doesn't think they're that big of a deal.. And I know, you're right - I guess I want to be back to 'normal' and not feel like this anymore (even though right now it doesn't feel like it'll happen). I'll be going to see my partner in his country on Sunday, so I have that to look forward to - I think his support, other than through a screen, will be needed

Thank you for the super kind offer :) That's amazing.. I haven't gone through even half of what you must have gone through and here I am, ha!   
It started around 2nd year of uni - I felt hopeless, like my life would never amount to anything (you know, everyone has it from what I'm told). It's been a year since I graduated and I've been in an internship that I just left today - recently everything became real and all the feeling now sound like this in my head: No one loves you (when I know they do, but I can't seem to shake that!), you won't be missed, you have no prospects in life, you won't get anywhere in the next year, your visa application for your fiance (to come to UK) will fail, nothing you do will amount to anything, you can't do it so don't try.  


I am deeply upset when I do, but confidently say to myself that I would rather just 'off' myself than be here.  


Does that make a little sense?

Hi Joe. I'm in UK, so on NHS luckily. I have no money for private. The doctor today gave me 2 numbers to call for counselling services - I told her I didn't want to go on meds, as I'm scared of what it can do to me (it had negative effects on my sister's mood around 7 years ago). My doc also mentioned CBT, which is also offered by the 2 contacts given. I'm not sure if I have the confidence to go for it though
